The *Mahāmoggallāna Sutta* (Ud 3.5; PTS Ud 27) is the fifth discourse of the third chapter (*Nanda Vagga*) of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. The sutta portrays the venerable Mahā Moggallāna engaged in meditation, which serves as the setting for an inspired utterance (*udāna*) [SuttaCentral]. The text is also cited in the *Peṭakopadesa* (*Ariyasaccappakāsanapaṭhamabhūmi*, Pe 1) [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations include an English version by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

While none of the surveyed secondary literature specifically examines this brief discourse, comparative analysis shows extensive textual relationships. Passage-level parallels to the verse are identified by SuttaCentral in various recensions of the *Udānavarga* and Chinese *Dharmapada* collections under the mindfulness/reflection chapter (*Smṛtivarga*), including Sanskrit versions (UV 15, UVS 15), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 15), and Chinese translations (T 210.6, T 212.16, and T 213.15) [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 27 matching passages across 12 texts, demonstrating shared formulaic prose frames depicting seated meditation and inspired utterances across the *Udāna*—notably with the immediately preceding *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 3.4, PTS Ud 27; §0.2–2.1 ↔ §0.2–2.1), the *Cūḷapanthaka Sutta* (Ud 5.10, PTS Ud 61; §0.1–2.1 ↔ §0.2–3.1), the *Sāriputtaupasama Sutta* (Ud 4.10), the *Kaṅkhārevata Sutta* (Ud 5.7), the *Piṇḍola Sutta* (Ud 4.6), the *Subhūti Sutta* (Ud 6.7), and the *Māra Saṁyutta* (SN 4) [DharmaNexus].
